source.title: Rethinking Benign Overfitting in Two-Layer Neural Networks

record.file_problem: The supplied text includes the full paper and appendices; no apparent garbling or cutoff affecting the reported results.
record.tranche_reason: The paper theoretically analyzes and experimentally evaluates how memorization of heterogeneous, class-dependent noise relates to test error, including test-error upper and lower bounds and data-removal experiments. These are conceptual tests of benign overfitting and memorization-related generalization, using a different data model and measures from the mapped claim versions.
record.gate_note: The synthetic-data test-accuracy heatmaps are described qualitatively in text, without extractable cell values. The MNIST noise-correlation heatmap is referenced but not described with specific result values in the supplied text. Figure 7's data-removal accuracy results are described qualitatively; no exact plotted values are stated. Prior-work results and comparisons mentioned in the introduction are not this study's results.
record.test_reason: The study analyzes benign overfitting with class-dependent feature noise, without testing fixed random-label fitting versus natural-label generalization (V1). Its removal experiments rank examples by covariance contribution, not by the memorization measure in V8, and compare high-score with low-score removal rather than random removal. No other version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that heterogeneous class-dependent noise can supply implicit features that improve long-tailed classification, derive conditional benign and harmful overfitting regimes, and propose a training-free covariance-based influence metric supported by synthetic and image-data experiments.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a class-dependent heterogeneous feature-noise model and two-layer ReLU CNNs trained with full-batch gradient descent; synthetic experiments use 20 epochs and report test accuracy, while the theory bounds zero-one test loss. This differs from the natural-label, random-label memorization settings in V1.
record.method_sensitivity: Test performance changes with feature strength, noise correlation ratio, dataset size, and whether data are long-tailed. The paper states test loss can be constant-order in the low signal-to-noise and low noise-correlation regime.

fits_no_version.finding: Under the paper's assumptions, two-layer ReLU CNNs attain arbitrarily small training loss; generalization depends on explicit feature strength and class-dependent noise correlations. Synthetic experiments qualitatively follow these dependencies.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Class-dependent feature noise can provide implicit predictive features, permitting benign overfitting on a model-defined long-tailed subset.

fits_no_version.finding: Removing examples contributing most to within-class covariance causes a larger reported accuracy drop than removing low-contribution examples.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: High covariance-contribution examples can matter more for image-classification accuracy than low-contribution examples.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning, Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 267, 2025
record.problems: The synthetic experimental results are presented as heatmaps and described qualitatively in the text, without numerical cell values. The real-world noise-correlation result is shown in a figure but no precise value or textual outcome is given here. The influence-removal results are also qualitative in the supplied text. The theoretical claims are conditional on the paper's data model and assumptions.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 3, Figure 4, Figure 6, and Figure 7 do not provide recoverable separate numeric values in the text; their described aggregate outcomes are represented in R1–R3 and R7–R9. No additional individual rows can be extracted without inventing values or assigning unreported outcomes.

untested.parts: Paired fixed random-label and natural-label training, near-perfect training fit, and held-out accuracy relative to chance.
Test error as width increases beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under specified tuning budgets.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness rankings of generalization gaps.
Removal ranked by measured label memorization versus equal-sized random removal, including the relative effect on MNIST.

record.verdict_notes: The original V1 verdicts conflate structured feature-noise learning with random-label memorization. The removal results resemble V8 conceptually, but the study does not validate its covariance score against V8's operational memorization measure or provide the required random-removal control. States marked cannot_determine concern the listed versions, not whether the study reports its own effects.

versions.untested_parts: Tests fitting the training data and benign versus harmful test loss under its own class-dependent feature-noise model. Does not test random-label fitting against natural-label generalization on CIFAR-10 or ImageNet using the specified architectures and recipes.

rows.subject: two-layer neural network
rows.operation_detail: Synthetic-data test accuracy as feature strength and noise correlation ratio vary; class dataset size fixed at 100.
rows.value: The test loss decreases with increasing feature strength and higher noise correlation ratios; with high noise correlation ratios, near-optimal test accuracy is achieved even when feature strength approaches nearly zero.
rows.note: Qualitative description of heatmap; no individual plotted values are stated.
rows.check: Measures generalization under class-dependent feature noise, without a random-label condition or the paired training-fit measurements required by V1. Figure 3 also includes uniform noise; this row covers only Gaussian noise.

rows.subject: two-layer neural network
rows.operation_detail: Synthetic-data test accuracy as noise correlation ratio and dataset size vary, with feature strength fixed.
rows.value: Test accuracy remains in a constant order with dataset size.
rows.note: Qualitative description; the text does not give accuracy values or identify a changing test-error gap.
rows.check: Constant-order accuracy as sample size varies is not partial evidence for V1; random-label fitting and generalization are not measured.

rows.subject: trained two-layer neural network
rows.operation_detail: Theorem bounds zero-one test loss under high signal-to-noise ratio for all data.

conditions.value: high signal-to-noise ratio: |Sk|²∥uk∥² ≥ C1·maxj≠k{|Sj|² A⊤k Aj F}

rows.uncertainty: with probability at least 1 − δ; constants C1 and c1 are absolute constants
rows.note: The paper calls this benign overfitting and states the trained network reaches optimal test loss in this regime.
rows.check: A theoretical bound under structured feature noise does not test V1. The extracted formula loses powers: the signal term is |Sk|²∥uk∥₂⁴ and the competing-noise term uses squared Frobenius norms. This is a theorem, not an empirical measurement.

rows.subject: trained two-layer neural network
rows.operation_detail: Theorem bounds zero-one test loss on long-tailed data under high noise-correlation ratio.

conditions.value: long-tailed data; |Sk|² A⊤k Ak F ≥ C2·maxj≠k{|Sj|² A⊤k Aj F}

rows.value: ≤ exp(−c2 L·|Sk|² A⊤k Ak F / maxj≠k{|Sj|² A⊤k Aj F})
rows.uncertainty: with probability at least 1 − δ; constants C2 and c2 are absolute constants
rows.note: The authors identify this as benign overfitting through learned class-dependent noise features.
rows.check: The conditional long-tailed-data bound does not test V1 or V8's removal comparison. The exponent contains L² and squared Frobenius norms, which the extraction omits. This is a theorem, not an empirical measurement.

rows.subject: trained two-layer neural network
rows.operation_detail: Theorem lower-bounds zero-one test loss when both signal-to-noise and noise-correlation ratios are small.

conditions.value: small signal-to-noise and noise-correlation ratios: |Sk|²∥uk∥² ≤ C3·maxj≠k{|Sj|² A⊤k Aj F} and |Sk|² A⊤k Ak F ≤ C3·maxj≠k{|Sj|² A⊤k Aj F}

rows.uncertainty: with probability at least 1 − δ; c3 is an absolute constant
rows.note: This is the paper's harmful-overfitting regime.
rows.check: A constant test-loss lower bound under this feature-noise model neither supports nor limits V1. The extracted conditions omit the fourth power of the feature norm and squares on Frobenius norms. This is a theorem, not an empirical measurement.
